question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
trigger: User explicitly requested $best-api-review audit annotations after querying the remaining ledger. Assessment and recording only; no product implementation.
requirements: Cover all six inventoried annotations source groups and materially different persistent, scoped, external-record, projected-view and paint consumers.
Preserve exact model/root and view identity, explicit anchor release, transaction rollback/expiry, and one canonical native mapping authority.
State deletion fallback and exact undo recovery truthfully without silently changing the same public policy merely because Authored is installed.
Keep external annotation/conversation lifetime separate from document writes, undo, inline paint and mounted view observation.
Use one document for a writer and a read-only reviewer of that same document; preserve independent view selection/focus.
Do not allocate or release retained editor resources inside replayable React state calculations; give resources explicit disposal ownership.
Retain settled Comments successor-lineage adoption, historical proof limits and separate feature scopes; no generic async framework or Widget carrier.
evidenceReuse: Inspected live native anchor construction/recovery, authored range bindings, annotation indexing/hooks, decoration compilation/observation, raw examples, Comments attachment/mapping, media and AI target lifetimes and Yjs point bindings. Independently reconciled April/May annotation history, August scoped-anchor implementation and September selection/Comments decisions and later execution. Replayed 107 core and 64 React baseline cases and a four-cohort public deletion/undo probe. Historical source-bound browser/performance claims remain historical; no new external research or native/browser replay.
summary: Pursue one consistent native deletion/recovery contract and remove the raw comment-mode consumer’s mirrored document, value-copy synchronization and duplicate anchors. Identical drop range calls collapse without exact recovery under ordinary mapping but become unavailable and recover exactly under Authored. Keep persistent/scoped lifetimes, reusable exact-view AnnotationStore/Provider and separate Decoration ownership; deleting the store would relocate its independent raw Plite job. Make React resource ownership explicit in the examples. Six semantic units and all six census groups reviewed, zero excluded and zero unresolved verdicts. Target runtime and adoption remain for Task design plan annotations.

reconciliation.reason: Static locations, exact selection and persistent/scoped targets still have independent jobs. The annotations review does not collapse their lifetimes or reintroduce universal locations.

reconciliation.reason: Retain deletion of the generic Widget carrier; direct semantic owners and exact-view geometry remain distinct. Old reference docs do not justify restoring Widget APIs.

reconciliation.reason: Retain one native model-owned target with resolve(view) and independent exact-view annotation indexes. Use this established capability to remove the raw demo replica topology.

reconciliation.reason: The provisional runtime status was subsequently resolved by the design-complete and implementation outcomes. Preserve its rejected per-read and per-binding candidates; do not treat the old Defer summary as current unimplemented work.

reconciliation.question: Which persistent anchor and transient annotation contracts can share native mapping without merging their lifetimes?
reconciliation.reason: Live source contains implemented successor lineage, ordinary replacement mapping and exact-view attachment ownership. Reopen only the cross-backend drop policy; retain nearest/Comments semantics and original proof limitations.

alternatives: Keep/configure: retain the existing annotation index, optional provider and separate decoration contract. Configuration cannot eliminate the same-document replica loop or reconcile the two drop policies.

Change existing native API: settle deletion fallback, retained target identity and exact undo recovery at editor.anchor/tx.anchor and their native owners. Uniform drop unavailability with exact undo recovery is a candidate; terminal-drop semantics must also be compared. No final signature or replacement runtime is accepted here.

Delete/merge at the consumer: replace two independent comment-mode documents with one model and separate mounted views; delete mirrorAnchor, repeated JSON/value replacement, duplicate source construction and per-comment synchronization. Reuse exact-view anchor resolution and keep per-view indexes.

Delete AnnotationStore/Provider or move it into Comments: reject. Raw Plite external semantic ranges are an independent current job; direct anchors lack collection indexing, keyed subscriptions, metadata comparison and external membership refresh. Feature-private copies relocate that work.

Merge anchors, annotations and decorations into one generic target store: reject. Transaction-scoped coordinates, durable identity, independently mutable semantic records and render attributes do not share lifetime or write authority.

Add anchor subscriptions, an async-result primitive or backend-mode flag: no proven missing capability in this audit. Existing feature generations, committed reads and decoration observation own async behavior; additional fan-out machinery requires its own evidence.

Move resource effects from React state updaters to explicit feature/event ownership and cleanup: pursue. The replica cut removes repeated mirror allocation; standalone persistent anchors still require owner disposal. No new global store or factory is justified.

Documentation-only reconciliation of drop: reject as the final target without choosing its native policy. Both implementations intentionally pass their own tests, yet the same public call has materially different deletion and recovery behavior. Preserve Comments nearest/succession law while reopening only this contract.

Replace the retained-target architecture or restore Widgets: reject. Later Comments execution adopted shared immutable lineage and exact-view resolution; the old deferred summary and obsolete docs are not evidence to reverse that implementation.
proofLimits: Baseline proof is 107/107 core tests and 64/64 React tests plus one public deletion/undo probe, recorded with source/runner fingerprints. No product code, candidate runtime, exact demo interaction, browser/device, collaboration or comparative scale certification. React updater allocation/disposal findings are source-backed hazards, not newly replayed reporter bugs. The proposed deletion law and one-model migration remain design/adoption work and need targeted behavior, locality and changed-runtime scale proof. Historical Aug23 execution remains unbound; later Comments receipts are reconciled without upgrading stale evidence or completing old plans.
